claims.feature: other: the record is unrevisable once printed
claims.claim: Wolfe says print cannot be revised: once it is out, it is out for all time.
claims.source: Gene Wolfe, written reply to Nigel Price, 'Gene Wolfe's time at Plant Engineering', Ultan's Library, 2013
claims.quote: There is no revising print
claims.page: Wolfe's reply to Price, first paragraph

claims.claim: Wolfe says he has never been able to catch and correct the printed assertion that he was editor of Plant Engineering, when he was a senior editor on the staff.
claims.source: Gene Wolfe, written reply to Nigel Price, 'Gene Wolfe's time at Plant Engineering', Ultan's Library, 2013
claims.quote: I was actually a senior editor on the staff
claims.page: Wolfe's reply to Price, first paragraph

claims.claim: Naming his Plant Engineering beats, Wolfe glosses each abstract department with a parenthesis of concrete objects.
claims.source: Gene Wolfe, written reply to Nigel Price, 'Gene Wolfe's time at Plant Engineering', Ultan's Library, 2013
claims.quote: (hydraulics, gears, pneumatics, belts, et cetera)
claims.page: Wolfe's reply to Price, second paragraph

claims.claim: Wolfe says a Plant Engineering senior editor had to supply cover articles, meaning write them and take the pictures himself.
claims.source: Gene Wolfe, written reply to Nigel Price, 'Gene Wolfe's time at Plant Engineering', Ultan's Library, 2013
claims.quote: meaning write the articles and take the pictures
claims.page: Wolfe's reply to Price, first paragraph

claims.feature: other: the record that does not survive
claims.claim: Wolfe says none of his Plant Engineering magazine articles have been reprinted anywhere.
claims.source: Gene Wolfe, written reply to Nigel Price, 'Gene Wolfe's time at Plant Engineering', Ultan's Library, 2013
claims.quote: none of my magazine articles have been reprinted anywhere

claims.claim: Ultan's Library dates Wolfe's Plant Engineering employment 1972 to 1984.
claims.source: Nigel Price, 'Gene Wolfe's time at Plant Engineering', Ultan's Library, 2013
claims.quote: worked (1972 – 1984) as an editor

claims.claim: Plant Engineering's own obituary of Wolfe dates his senior editorship 1972 to 1986, four years later than the terminal date Ultan's Library gives.
claims.source: Bob Vavra, 'Gene Wolfe: 1931-2019', Plant Engineering, 2019
claims.quote: senior editor of Plant Engineering magazine from 1972 to 1986
claims.confidence: high: the figure is on the page; the conflict with ultan.org.uk/plant-engineering/ is stated by comparison of the two pages, both fetched

claims.claim: Wolfe says being the Letters to the Editor editor at Plant Engineering was good and fun and taught him a lot of stuff.
claims.source: Gene Wolfe, interviewed by Lawrence Person, 'Suns New, Long, and Short', Nova Express Vol 5 No 1, Fall/Winter 1998 (blog reprint 2021)
claims.quote: which was good and fun and taught me a lot

claims.claim: Asked to name the best editors he had worked with, Wolfe named David Hartwell first and called him his principal editor.
claims.source: Gene Wolfe, interviewed by Lawrence Person, 'Suns New, Long, and Short', Nova Express Vol 5 No 1, Fall/Winter 1998 (blog reprint 2021)
claims.quote: He's been my principal editor over the years

claims.claim: Wolfe placed Damon Knight second among the editors he had worked with, after Hartwell.
claims.source: Gene Wolfe, interviewed by Lawrence Person, 'Suns New, Long, and Short', Nova Express Vol 5 No 1, Fall/Winter 1998 (blog reprint 2021)
claims.quote: Damon Knight would have to come in second

claims.claim: Wolfe says Hartwell asked him to add a closing paragraph stating that Severian leaves Urth and saves the sun.
claims.source: Gene Wolfe, interviewed by Lawrence Person, 'Suns New, Long, and Short', Nova Express Vol 5 No 1, Fall/Winter 1998 (blog reprint 2021)
claims.quote: David Hartwell said that I should put a paragraph in at the end
claims.page: answer on Urth of the New Sun

claims.claim: Wolfe answered his editor that the requested closing paragraph was more than a paragraph.
claims.source: Gene Wolfe, interviewed by Lawrence Person, 'Suns New, Long, and Short', Nova Express Vol 5 No 1, Fall/Winter 1998 (blog reprint 2021)
claims.quote: David, that's more than a paragraph.
claims.page: answer on Urth of the New Sun

claims.claim: Wolfe says he wrote The Urth of the New Sun to answer what had happened to the people and the places of the tetralogy.
claims.source: Gene Wolfe, interviewed by Lawrence Person, 'Suns New, Long, and Short', Nova Express Vol 5 No 1, Fall/Winter 1998 (blog reprint 2021)
claims.quote: what happened to all these people, what happened to all these places
claims.page: answer on Urth of the New Sun

claims.claim: Dirda reports that every one of Wolfe's stories and novels goes through at least three drafts and occasionally as many as ten.
claims.source: Michael Dirda, reporting, The Washington Post Book World, 30 January 1983
claims.quote: at least three drafts, occasionally as many as 10
claims.routeHint: gwern.net plain-text transcript of the Washington Post piece

claims.claim: Dirda reports that at Plant Engineering Wolfe bought some twenty-five free-lanced articles a year.
claims.source: Michael Dirda, reporting, The Washington Post Book World, 30 January 1983
claims.quote: buys some 25 free-lanced articles a year

claims.claim: Dirda reports that Wolfe wrote a major cover story for Plant Engineering every few months while writing The Book of the New Sun.
claims.source: Michael Dirda, reporting, The Washington Post Book World, 30 January 1983
claims.quote: writes a major cover story every few months

claims.claim: Wolfe says he is never sure he is through with a manuscript until he mails it out.
claims.source: Gene Wolfe, interviewed by Michael Dirda, The Washington Post Book World, 30 January 1983
claims.quote: Until I mail a manuscript out I'm never sure

claims.feature: other: what an editor made of him
claims.claim: Wolfe says his dedication of The Fifth Head of Cerberus to Damon Knight commemorates Knight growing him from a bean.
claims.source: Gene Wolfe, interviewed by Michael Dirda, The Washington Post Book World, 30 January 1983
claims.quote: when he grew me from a bean

claims.feature: other: what an editor made of him
claims.claim: Dirda describes Damon Knight as a mentor to many contemporary science fiction writers.
claims.source: Michael Dirda, reporting, The Washington Post Book World, 30 January 1983
claims.quote: a mentor to many contemporary science fiction writers

claims.claim: Wolfe told Damon Knight that the books which influenced him were Tolkien, Chesterton and the standard handbook of mechanical engineering.
claims.source: Gene Wolfe, interviewed by Michael Dirda, The Washington Post Book World, 30 January 1983
claims.quote: the much neglected G.K. Chesterton, and the standard handbook

claims.claim: Tor.com's obituary gives Wolfe's answer to Knight about his biggest influences as Chesterton and Marks' Standard Handbook for Mechanical Engineers, without the Tolkien that Wolfe named to Dirda in 1983.
claims.source: Tor.com editorial staff, 'Author and Grand Master Gene Wolfe, 1931-2019', 15 April 2019 (Reactor)
claims.quote: Chesterton and Marks’ [Standard] Handbook for [Mechanical] Engineers
claims.confidence: medium: the page is an unsourced secondhand rendering of the anecdote; the Tolkien difference is established by comparison with the Dirda transcript

claims.feature: other: an editor changing the form not the sentences
claims.claim: Wolfe says Damon Knight liked 'Trip, Trap' but not its double-column format, and asked him to break it into conventional alternating sections.
claims.source: Gene Wolfe, Contemporary Authors Autobiography Series Vol. 9, quoted on WolfeWiki
claims.quote: Knight liked the story but not its double-column format
claims.page: 'A note about the writing of the story'
claims.confidence: high: Wolfe's own words, but reached through WolfeWiki's transcription of Contemporary Authors Autobiography Series Vol. 9

claims.feature: other: an editor marking the cut points
claims.claim: Wolfe says Knight returned the story marked to show the points at which he felt the switches from one letter to the other should be made.
claims.source: Gene Wolfe, Contemporary Authors Autobiography Series Vol. 9, quoted on WolfeWiki
claims.quote: marked to show the points at which he felt
claims.page: 'A note about the writing of the story'
claims.confidence: high: Wolfe's own words via WolfeWiki's transcription of CAAS vol. 9

claims.feature: other: an editor marking the cut points
claims.claim: Wolfe says he spent a couple of hours trying to improve on Knight's marked switch points and found he could not.
claims.source: Gene Wolfe, Contemporary Authors Autobiography Series Vol. 9, quoted on WolfeWiki
claims.quote: I spent a couple of hours trying to improve
claims.page: 'A note about the writing of the story'
claims.confidence: high: Wolfe's own words via WolfeWiki's transcription of CAAS vol. 9

claims.claim: Hartwell says Gene Wolfe is the writer with whom he had an editorial relationship for the majority of his career.
claims.source: David G. Hartwell, tribute in the Chicago Literary Hall of Fame Fuller Award program for Gene Wolfe, 2012
claims.quote: relationship for the majority of my career, longer than with any other
claims.page: Fuller Award program, tributes section (p. 18-19 of the program)

claims.claim: Hartwell says part of his reputation as an editor derives from the fact that he is Gene Wolfe's editor.
claims.source: David G. Hartwell, tribute in the Chicago Literary Hall of Fame Fuller Award program for Gene Wolfe, 2012
claims.quote: part of my reputation as an editor derives
claims.page: Fuller Award program, tributes section (p. 18-19 of the program)

claims.claim: Cooney reports Wolfe's standing advice to tell a story as cleanly and as clearly as possible.
claims.source: Gene Wolfe, quoted from memory by C. S. E. Cooney, Ultan's Library, 2016
claims.quote: tell a story as cleanly and as clearly as possible

claims.claim: Cooney says Wolfe's letter on her chapters named what she was doing well, dialogue and character, as well as the fault.
claims.source: C. S. E. Cooney, 'An Homage to my Honorary Grandfather', Ultan's Library, 2016
claims.quote: what I was doing well (Dialogue! Character!)

claims.claim: Cooney reports Wolfe agreeing to read her novel while refusing to promise any comment on it.
claims.source: C. S. E. Cooney, 'An Homage to my Honorary Grandfather', Ultan's Library, 2016
claims.quote: I can read it, but I can’t promise to say anything

claims.claim: Cooney reports Wolfe ranking the forms by difficulty, novels easiest, short stories harder, poetry hardest.
claims.source: Gene Wolfe, quoted from memory by C. S. E. Cooney, Ultan's Library, 2016
claims.quote: novels are the easiest to write. Short stories are harder

claims.claim: Cooney reports Wolfe saying anything can be a short story and instancing the chair and the waiter in front of them.
claims.source: Gene Wolfe, quoted from memory by C. S. E. Cooney, Ultan's Library, 2016
claims.quote: This chair could be a short story. That waiter

claims.claim: Cooney says Wolfe told her that he too overwrites his early drafts.
claims.source: C. S. E. Cooney, 'An Homage to my Honorary Grandfather', Ultan's Library, 2016
claims.quote: Gene told me he does too
claims.page: memoir, on lumps of uncooked prose

claims.claim: Cooney reports Wolfe describing the last pass on a finished story as grooming it before sending it out again.
claims.source: Gene Wolfe, quoted from memory by C. S. E. Cooney, Ultan's Library, 2016
claims.quote: Scrub her face. Give her a new dress.

claims.claim: Cooney reports Wolfe's rule that writers who do not subscribe to the magazines they submit to are cutting their own throats.
claims.source: Gene Wolfe, quoted from memory by C. S. E. Cooney, Ultan's Library, 2016
claims.quote: are cutting their own throats
